\section{Overview}

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Expectation against a linear form]
\lean{FABL.expect_mul_linearForm_eq_singletonCoeffs}
\label{FABL.expect_mul_linearForm_eq_singletonCoeffs}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.linearForm, FABL.monomial}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, and let $a$ assign a real coefficient to each coordinate. The uniform
expectation of $f(x)$ times the linear form $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$ equals $\sum_{i=1}^n
a_i\widehat f(\{i\})$, where $\widehat f(\{i\})$ is the uniform expectation of
$f(x)x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound by a threshold and positive part]
\lean{FABL.mul_le_threshold_add_posPart}
\label{FABL.mul_le_threshold_add_posPart}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every $r,y,t\in\mathbb{R}$ with $0\le r\le 1$, one has $ry\le tr+\max(y-t,0)$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{6}
For every real $\alpha$ with $0<\alpha<1/2$, there is a constant $C_\alpha>0$ such that
the following holds for every integer $n\ge0$. Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ satisfy
$0\le f(x)\le1$ for every $x$, have uniform-cube mean at most $\alpha$, and have each
first-level Fourier coefficient of absolute value at most $\varepsilon$, where
$\varepsilon\ge0$. Then the sum of the squares of its first-level Fourier coefficients
is at most $I(\alpha)^2+C_\alpha\varepsilon$, where $I(\alpha)$ is the standard Gaussian
density evaluated at the real number whose standard Gaussian upper-tail probability is
$\alpha$.
\end{theorem}
